questions.q: What does reappraisal involve before a big performance?
a: Relabeling nervous energy as excitement
Forcing yourself to feel completely calm
Ignoring the physical signs of stress
Rehearsing your material one final time
questions.why: Lesson 1 says you cannot stop the stress hormones, but you can turn anxiety into excitement by reappraising it.

questions.q: Why is shifting from nerves to excitement easier than shifting to calm?
a: Worry and excitement sit closer together emotionally
Excitement requires no physical arousal at all
Calm can only be reached through long practice
Nervousness disappears once the event begins
questions.why: Lesson 1 says anxious and calm are very different states, while worried and excited are close enough to swap easily.

questions.q: How does the centering technique work?
a: Breathe deeply, release tension and gather energy at the belly
Tense every muscle, then stand up and shake it off
Picture the audience succeeding alongside you
Repeat a single word until your mind goes blank
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes centering as deep breathing, releasing muscle tension and visualizing energy at the belly button.

questions.q: What did the golf club study suggest?
a: Belief in a club's history improved players' scores
Expensive clubs always outperform cheaper ones
Golfers play worse when they feel observed
Practice matters far more than any equipment
questions.why: Lesson 2 says golfers told the clubs belonged to pros performed better, because the belief alone helped them.

questions.q: What did T-Mobile's ads attacking bigger rivals achieve?
a: They won customers by casting the firm as the underdog
They forced rivals to lower their prices
They made the brand seem more premium
They ended the company's financial losses at once
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the campaign increased competition and led people to root for the underdog, helping save the company.
